Stair company adds centralized wood dust collection system
November 13, 2026 | 11:17 am CST
Stair company adds centralized wood dust collection system
WHITING, N.J. — DMD Stairs has equipped its new woodworking facility with a centralized wood dust collection system designed and installed by Clean Air Company of Fords, New Jersey.

Built around a Coral FM READY modular sleeve dust collector from Coral USA, the industrial dust collection system captures dust and wood chips at each piece of woodworking equipment and carries the material through overhead ductwork to a single, centralized collector located inside the building.

DMD Stairs fabricates custom staircases and railings for residential and commercial projects. When the company moved to its new shop, it needed a dust collection system tailored to its machinery and floor plan that wouldn’t sacrifice space needed for fabrication. Clean Air Company evaluated the shop layout, woodworking equipment, and expected airflow requirements before engineering a wood dust collection system specifically for the facility.

Cutting, shaping, and sanding wood in a stair and railing workshop generate significant amounts of wood dust and chips. Without source capture, fine particles and chips settle on machinery and floors, increasing cleanup time and creating machine maintenance issues. The source-capture system installed by Clean Air Company collects the material directly from each machine through customized hood connections, branch lines, and anti-static flex hose. Overhead galvanized-steel ductwork carries the captured dust and chips to a centrally located dust collector. Routing the ductwork overhead keeps floor space available for production materials and finished products. The collected material empties into collection bins for removal, and airflow controls regulate air movement through the system.

The Coral FM READY is a compact, enclosureless sleeve dust collector intended for wood dust and small-chip applications under 5,000 CFM. Its filter sleeves provide filtration area within a small equipment footprint. DMD Stairs selected the unit based on its specifications and price. The collector provides centralized dust collection without the space requirements of a larger outdoor unit or a separate storage silo.

The system was designed for airflow below 5,000 CFM and reviewed in relation to applicable requirements governing indoor enclosureless wood dust collectors, including equipment configuration, safety considerations, and installation location. Locating the unit indoors reduced project costs and provided easier access for inspection, maintenance, and material removal.

Wood dust is combustible and can present fire and deflagration hazards. Clean Air Company designed the system to meet the applicable requirements of NFPA 660, the consolidated combustible dust standard that now incorporates the safety provisions previously published in NFPA 652. The design also follows applicable International Mechanical Code provisions. NFPA 660 addresses hazard assessment, ignition-source control, dust accumulation, equipment design, and fire or explosion protection.

Clean Air Company handled the project from design and equipment selection through ductwork layout and installation. With one company responsible for all phases, the collector, duct system, and machine connections were coordinated around DMD Stairs’ new production layout.

“DMD Stairs needed dust collection that fit their new shop and the workflow of their team,” said Greg Slavin, president of Clean Air Company. “The Coral FM READY gave them centralized collection in a compact package.”
